primitives.name: Motion-to-Event Projection
primitives.verbatim_quote: We introduce event projection heads that explicitly connect player movements to basketball events like passes, shots, and steals, training the model to associate physical motion patterns with their tactical purposes.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p_{t,i}': 'player position at time t, i-th player (meters)', 'n_{t,i}': 'shoulder normal vector at time t, i-th player (dimensionless)', 's_{t,i}': 'encoded motion state at time t, i-th player (dimensionless)', 'E': 'event class set {pass, shot, steal, etc.}', 'f_{\\text{proj}}': 'projection function mapping motion to event (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Player motion is deterministic within local temporal frame; event classification is invariant to global positional shifts.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When motion patterns lack semantic signal (e.g., random jitter), projection accuracy degrades.

layer2.mapping: Maps 3D joint trajectories and body orientation to discrete event classes via learned embedding space.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-entropy loss on projected event labels during fine-tuning.

primitives.name: Graph Neural Motion Encoder
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our two-stage approach first processes skeletal tracking data through Graph Neural Networks to capture nuanced motion patterns, then employs a Transformer architecture with specialized attention mechanisms to model player interactions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'J_{i,j,k,t}': '3D joint coordinates for player i, joint j, time t (meters)', 'G = (V,E)': 'graph structure of players and inter-player relationships (dimensionless)', 'H^{(l)}': 'hidden representation at layer l (dimensionless)', 'W^{(l)}': 'learned weight matrix at layer l (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Players form a static graph; motion dynamics are Markovian within short time windows.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when player connectivity changes abruptly or motion is too sparse.

layer2.mapping: Encodes temporal sequences of skeletal data into relational motion kernels via GNN message passing.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error between predicted and actual joint positions.

primitives.name: Transformer Player Interaction Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our two-stage approach first processes skeletal tracking data through Graph Neural Networks to capture nuanced motion patterns, then employs a Transformer architecture with specialized attention mechanisms to model player interactions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'X_{t,i}': 'input token for player i at time t (dimensionless)', 'A_{ij}^{(t)}': 'attention weight between players i and j at time t (dimensionless)', 'Q, K, V': 'query, key, value matrices (dimensionless)', 'Z_{t,i}': 'output representation for player i at time t (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Player interactions can be modeled as pairwise attention; temporal dependencies are captured via causal masking.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Attention collapses when input tokens are insufficiently informative or when long-range dependencies exceed model capacity.

layer2.mapping: Models multi-agent spatiotemporal dynamics via self-attention over player states.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of predicted next-step player positions based on attention-weighted interaction maps.

reasoning_traces.think:
CourtMotion leverages skeletal tracking data to extract motion features that encode both kinematic behavior and semantic intent. The GNN stage encodes spatial relationships among joints into a latent motion kernel, capturing posture and preparatory gestures missed by traditional position-only models. This is followed by a Transformer module that models temporal evolution and inter-player coordination through attention mechanisms. The event projection heads link these representations to specific basketball actions—such as passes, shots, or steals—by learning mappings from motion features to event classes. The dual nature of this framework allows it to anticipate future game states not just through positional prediction but also through interpretation of motion semantics. Failure modes arise when motion lacks discriminative signal or when attention fails to resolve complex multi-agent dynamics. The system thus operates under a dual regime: one where motion is predictive of outcome, and another where it reflects tactical awareness.
